name: Jollof Rice and Chicken
feedback_template: Your jollof rice and chicken was tasty!  This meal gives you good energy from carbs and protein from the chicken. The tomato base is rich in lycopene — a powerful antioxidant. Next time, try adding steamed vegetables or a side salad for extra fibre and vitamins.
insight: Jollof gives you steady energy from rice, and the chicken tops it up with lean protein.

name: Eba and Egusi Soup
feedback_template: Nice one! Egusi is packed with healthy fats and protein from melon seeds.  To balance the heavy carbs in eba, try a smaller portion of eba next time and add more dark leafy greens to the soup. The iron in the vegetables helps your body absorb nutrients better.
insight: Egusi is rich in healthy fats and plant protein from melon seeds.

name: Moi Moi and Plantain
feedback_template: You're doing well! Moi moi is an excellent source of plant protein and fibre.  Paired with plantain, you get good energy and potassium. If the plantain was fried, try boiling or roasting it next time for a lighter meal. Great combo!
insight: Moi moi is an excellent source of plant protein and fibre.

name: Beans and Fried Plantain
feedback_template: Great choice! Beans give you lasting energy and fibre — they're one of the best plant protein sources out there.  The fried plantain adds nice flavour, but boiling or roasting it could make this a clean 10/10. Try adding a sprinkle of onions and tomatoes on the side!
insight: Beans give you lasting energy and fibre — one of the best plant proteins.

name: Ugwu Soup and Fufu
feedback_template: Awesome! Ugwu leaves are a powerhouse of iron and vitamins A & C.  This is a wonderfully nourishing meal that supports your energy and immune system. Fufu gives sustained energy. Consider adding a protein source like fish or chicken to make it a complete meal.
insight: Ugwu leaves are a powerhouse of iron and vitamins A and C.

name: Suya
feedback_template: Suya is a fantastic high-protein snack — the spice blend (yaji) contains ginger and pepper which have anti-inflammatory properties.  Just remember to pair it with some cabbage, tomatoes, and onions to balance the spice and add fresh vitamins. A squeeze of lemon goes a long way!
insight: Suya is a fantastic high-protein snack with anti-inflammatory spices.

name: Amala and Ewedu Soup
feedback_template: A Yoruba classic! Ewedu is loaded with vitamins A, C, and E plus iron and calcium.  Amala from yam flour provides good carbs. To boost this meal, add more protein with stewed chicken or fish. The combination of ewedu and gbegiri is a nutrient powerhouse!
insight: Ewedu is loaded with vitamins A, C and E plus iron and calcium.

name: Pounded Yam and Ogbono Soup
feedback_template: Ogbono (wild mango) soup is rich in healthy fats and helps lower cholesterol.  Pounded yam is filling and energising. For a more balanced meal, try adding more vegetables to the soup and reducing the yam portion slightly. Great cultural food!
insight: Ogbono soup is rich in healthy fats and helps support good cholesterol.

name: Noodles (Indomie)
feedback_template: We get it — Indomie hits different!  It's quick and tasty, but it's high in sodium and refined carbs. To make it healthier, crack an egg into it, add some sliced cabbage, carrots, or spinach. Skip the seasoning packet and use half — you'll cut sodium by 50%.
insight: Quick and tasty, but high in sodium — add an egg and veggies to balance it.

name: Pepper Soup
feedback_template: Pepper soup is light, warming, and great for hydration!  The spices like uziza, ehuru, and ogiri have traditional medicinal benefits. If it's goat meat pepper soup, you're getting lean protein. Pair with a small portion of rice or yam for a complete meal. Well done!
insight: Light, warming and great for hydration, with traditional medicinal spices.

name: Fried Rice
feedback_template: Fried rice is tasty and versatile!  The mixed vegetables add vitamins and fibre. However, the oil used in frying can pile up calories. Try stir-frying with less oil, and add more vegetables than rice. Chicken or shrimp protein on top makes it a well-rounded meal.
insight: Colourful and tasty — the vegetables add fibre and vitamins.

name: Yam and Egg Sauce
feedback_template: Yam is a great source of complex carbs and potassium!  The eggs add quality protein. To level up, add tomatoes, peppers, and onions to the sauce for extra vitamins. Boiling the yam instead of frying saves calories while keeping all the nutrients.
insight: Yam gives sustained energy — egg sauce adds quality protein.

name: Bread and Tea
feedback_template: A Nigerian breakfast staple!  If you're using whole wheat bread, that's great fibre. The tea (especially if it's milo or hot chocolate) adds some energy. Try adding boiled eggs or akara for protein — it'll keep you fuller longer and prevent that mid-morning crash.
insight: Bread and tea is a classic start — wholegrain bread keeps you fuller longer.

name: Akara and Pap
feedback_template: A perfect Nigerian breakfast! Akara is made from beans — excellent plant protein and fibre.  Pap (ogi) is light and easy to digest. Together they give you balanced energy. If the akara was deep-fried, try air-frying or baking for a lighter version. Solid choice!
insight: Akara is a brilliant plant-protein breakfast — crisp, filling and affordable.

name: Ofada Rice and Ayamase
feedback_template: Ofada rice is unpolished, which means it retains more fibre, vitamins, and minerals than regular white rice!  Ayamase (green pepper stew) is rich in peppers and spices. Watch the oil content though — the traditional recipe can be heavy. A smaller portion of sauce with more rice balances it out.
insight: Ofada rice is wholegrain — the ayamase adds bold, rich flavour.

name: Banga Soup and Starch
feedback_template: Banga (palm fruit) soup is rich in beta-carotene and healthy fats.  It's a Niger Delta delicacy! The starch (from cassava) is filling. To make it more balanced, add fish or chicken for protein and pair with a side of vegetables. The spices in banga have anti-inflammatory benefits!
insight: Banga soup is rich in palm fruit goodness and traditional flavour.

name: Chicken and Chips
feedback_template: The chicken is a great lean protein source!  The chips (if baked) are a reasonable carb. If deep-fried, the oil content goes up. Try oven-baked chips with skin-on for extra fibre, and add a side of coleslaw or grilled vegetables. The protein-to-carb ratio is solid!
insight: A filling favourite — try oven chips and a side salad to lighten it.

name: Spaghetti (Pasta)
feedback_template: Pasta gives you quick energy from carbs.  To make it more nutritious, add a protein source like chicken, fish, or eggs, and load up on vegetables — tomatoes, peppers, spinach, or mixed veg. Whole wheat pasta has more fibre and keeps you fuller longer.
insight: Pasta gives quick energy — load it with veggies and lean protein.

name: Okra Soup and Fufu
feedback_template: Okra is a fibre superstar and contains vitamins A, C, and K!  It also has folate and is great for gut health. Combined with fufu for carbs, this is a solid meal. Add more protein — fish, goat meat, or shrimp — to make it a complete balanced plate.
insight: Okra is packed with fibre and vitamins — great for digestion.

name: Tuwo Shinkafa and Miyan Kuka
feedback_template: A Northern Nigerian classic! Tuwo shinkafa (rice pudding) is soft and easy to digest.  Miyan kuka (baobab leaf soup) is incredibly nutritious — rich in vitamin C, calcium, and antioxidants. Baobab is a superfood! Add some protein like beef or fish for a complete meal.
insight: Baobab leaf soup (kuka) is rich in calcium and vitamin C.

name: Banku and Tilapia
feedback_template: Banku is a fermented corn and cassava dough — the fermentation adds probiotics for gut health!  Tilapia is lean protein with omega-3 fatty acids. This combo is well-balanced. Add some shito (black pepper sauce) and fresh tomatoes for extra flavour and vitamins. Solid Ghana-Naija fusion!
insight: Banku is fermented and gut-friendly — tilapia adds lean protein.

name: Garri (Eba) and Stew
feedback_template: Garri is quick energy from cassava — it's filling and affordable.  The stew adds flavour and nutrients from tomatoes and peppers. To boost this meal, add a protein source like chicken, fish, or egg to the stew. More vegetables in the stew = more vitamins!
insight: Garri gives quick energy — add plenty of stew protein and greens.

name: Fruit Salad
feedback_template: Excellent choice!  Fresh fruits are packed with vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. Nigerian fruits like pawpaw, watermelon, pineapple, and oranges are incredible for hydration and immunity. If you added yogurt, that's bonus probiotics. This is one of the healthiest snacks you can have!
insight: A colourful fruit bowl is a vitamin-packed, refreshing choice.

name: Ofada Stew
feedback_template: Ofada stew (ayamase) is rich in green peppers and traditional spices.  It's protein-packed when made with assorted meat and eggs. Watch the palm oil quantity — it's nutrient-dense but calorie-heavy. Pair with ofada rice (unpolished) for maximum fibre and nutrients!
insight: Ayamase-style stew is rich and smoky — enjoy with wholegrain ofada rice.

name: Jollof Spaghetti
feedback_template: Jollof spaghetti is a fun twist on the classic!  The tomato-based sauce adds lycopene and vitamin C. To make it healthier, add mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, peas) and a protein like chicken or shrimp. Use whole wheat spaghetti for extra fibre if available.
insight: Party jollof spaghetti — add vegetables and protein to balance it.

name: Chin Chin
feedback_template: Chin chin is a beloved snack!  It's crunchy and satisfying, but it's deep-fried and can be high in sugar and fat. Enjoy a small handful as a treat rather than a meal. Pair it with fruit or yogurt to balance it out. Everything in moderation!
insight: Sweet and crunchy — enjoy a small handful, it is easy to overdo.

name: Puff Puff
feedback_template: Puff puff is pure comfort!  These fried dough balls are delicious but calorie-dense. They're mostly carbs and fat with minimal protein or vitamins. Enjoy 2-3 pieces as a treat, not a full meal. Pair with fruit or a protein source to make it more balanced.
insight: Soft, golden and loved by all — a weekend treat to share.

name: Asun (Spicy Goat Meat)
feedback_template: Asun is high in protein and iron from goat meat!  The spicy pepper marinade has capsaicin which boosts metabolism. Pair with a fresh salad or sautéed vegetables for fibre and vitamins. Goat meat is leaner than beef — great protein choice for a snack or light meal!
insight: Asun is bold, spicy and high in protein — great with veggies.

name: Couscous and Vegetable Stew
feedback_template: Couscous is a light grain that cooks quickly and pairs well with stews.  The vegetable stew adds vitamins A, C, and K plus fibre. To boost protein, add chickpeas, chicken, or fish. This is a balanced, light meal — great for lunch or dinner!
insight: Light and colourful — couscous with vegetable stew is easy on the stomach.

name: Ewa Agoyin
feedback_template: Ewa agoyin — soft beans with spicy palm oil sauce — is a Lagos street food staple!  Beans are an excellent source of protein and fibre. The palm oil sauce adds flavour but is calorie-dense. Enjoy this as an occasional treat, and add a side of bread or yam for balance.
insight: Ewa agoyin is a smoky bean classic — beans are fibre and protein heroes.

name: Apple
feedback_template: Apples are fibre-rich, hydrating and make a perfect intentional snack. Apples can help reduce risk of developing diabetes and heart disease!
insight: Apples can help reduce the risk of developing diabetes and heart disease!

name: Banana
feedback_template: Bananas are a great quick energy source, rich in potassium for muscle and heart health.
insight: Bananas are packed with potassium, which supports your heart and muscles.

name: Orange
feedback_template: Oranges are bursting with vitamin C — a simple immunity boost for your day.
insight: Oranges are rich in vitamin C, supporting your immune system.

name: Avocado
feedback_template: Avocado is full of healthy monounsaturated fats that keep you full and support your heart.
insight: Avocado's healthy fats keep you full longer and support heart health.

name: Bread
feedback_template: Bread gives quick energy — go for wholegrain or sourdough when you can.
insight: Wholegrain bread provides steady energy and more fibre than white.

name: Boiled Eggs
feedback_template: Eggs are a complete protein — one of the most affordable quality proteins around.
insight: Eggs are a complete protein and one of the most affordable quality sources.

name: Grilled Chicken
feedback_template: Grilled chicken is lean, high-quality protein — grilled beats fried every time.
insight: Grilled chicken is lean protein that helps build and repair muscle.

name: White Rice
feedback_template: Rice is a reliable energy source — pair it with protein and veggies for balance.
insight: Rice fuels your day — add protein and vegetables to round it out.

name: Green Salad
feedback_template: A fresh salad is a fibre and vitamin goldmine — keep the dressing light.
insight: Leafy salads are full of fibre and vitamins with very few calories.

name: Fried Fish
feedback_template: Fish is rich in omega-3 — grilling or steaming keeps it healthier than frying.
insight: Fish is rich in omega-3 fats that are brilliant for your heart.

name: Yam
feedback_template: Yam is a filling, traditional carb — pair it with a protein-rich sauce.
insight: Yam gives you lasting energy and is rich in fibre and potassium.

name: Fruit Smoothie
feedback_template: A smoothie is a tasty way to hit your fruit goals — skip the added sugar.
insight: Smoothies are a delicious way to pack in fruit — hold the added sugar.

name: Frittata
feedback_template: A frittata is a protein-packed way to use up seasonal vegetables.
insight: Frittatas are protein-packed and perfect for using seasonal vegetables.

name: Groundnut Soup
feedback_template: Groundnut soup is rich and warming — a little goes a long way nutritionally.
insight: Groundnut soup is energy-dense with healthy fats and plant protein.

name: Oatmeal
feedback_template: Oatmeal is a heart-friendly breakfast that keeps you full till lunch.
insight: Oatmeal's soluble fibre supports heart health and steady energy.

name: Cucumber
feedback_template: Cucumber is hydrating and refreshing — a crunchy, low-calorie snack.
insight: Cucumbers are mostly water — perfect for hydration and crunch.
